curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Addition Adventure!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome kindergarten learners to the joy of addition. Introduce our three core missions: joining groups of fun physical objects to find totals within 5 to 10, recognizing our math power tools (the plus sign '+' and equals sign '='), and discovering how putting things together makes bigger amounts.

components.intent: Help students physically place two colored sets of counters into a ten-frame grid to visualize combining two distinct groups into one whole group.

components.title: Meet the Math Signs
components.intent: Introduce the plus sign (+) as the symbol that puts groups together and the equal sign (=) as the symbol showing the total or same amount, using kid-friendly character art and visual cues.

components.title: Explore the Signs
components.intent: Let learners tap and inspect the plus sign (+) and equal sign (=) in a simple visual equation layout to learn their names, meanings, and jobs in an addition sentence.

components.title: Put the Signs in Place
components.intent: Invite kindergarteners to drag the plus (+) and equal (=) signs into simple illustrated number sentences to see how they connect groups to their total.

data.title: The Growing Treasure Basket: Hands-On Adding Fun!
data.subject: Math
data.overview: Embark on a treasure-gathering adventure around the house with your helper! By combining small groups of everyday toys into one shared basket, learners visually discover how addition brings sets together to make a bigger total.
learningObjectives: Model addition by joining two distinct groups of physical objects together.
Count with 1-to-1 correspondence up to 10 to find the total sum.
Explain orally that adding more items makes a collection grow larger.

substitutes: Taped square zones on the table or floor

steps.title: Set Up the Counting Islands
steps.instruction: Lay two paper plates side-by-side on your table or floor, and set the empty treasure basket right behind them.
steps.tip: Leaving space between the two plates helps your eyes see two distinct groups clearly before we combine them.

steps.title: Build Your First Treasure Group
steps.instruction: Pick one type of item (like 3 rolled socks or 3 crayons) and place them onto the left plate, counting aloud as you place each one: 'One, two, three!'

checkpoint.question: How many items are sitting on the left plate right now?

steps.scienceNote: When we touch each item while saying its number, that is called one-to-one correspondence. It ensures no object is missed or counted twice.

steps.title: Build Your Partner's Treasure Group
steps.instruction: Have your adult helper place 2 different items (like 2 plastic blocks) onto the right plate, counting aloud together: 'One, two!'

checkpoint.question: Are both plates ready with their own groups of treasures?

steps.title: Merge the Treasures Together
steps.instruction: Gently slide or dump the 3 items from the left plate into the basket, then add the 2 items from the right plate into the same basket!
steps.tip: Say the magic math word 'PLUS' or 'AND' as you slide the second group into the basket.

steps.title: Count the Big Treasure Pile
steps.instruction: Reach into the basket and pull the objects out one by one, lining them up to find out the new total.

checkpoint.question: How many treasures are in your combined pile now?

steps.scienceNote: Addition means joining groups together. When we combine two positive groups, the total group becomes bigger than each separate group was at the start.

steps.title: Record the Story in Pictures
steps.instruction: On your paper, draw simple circles for your 3 treasures, draw a plus sign (+), draw 2 more circles, and draw the total number (5) at the end!

checkpoint.question: Does the basket have more treasures than one plate had by itself?

steps.tip: Keep drawings quick and simple! Dots, stars, or smiley faces work great for kindergarten math stories.

reflectionPrompts.question: When you poured both plates into the basket, what happened to the size of the treasure pile?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Explain orally that adding more items makes a collection grow larger.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about whether the basket looked fuller or emptier after bringing both sets together.

reflectionPrompts.question: If you put 4 socks in the basket and your helper gives you 0 socks, how many socks are in the basket?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Model addition by joining two distinct groups of physical objects together.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Does adding nothing change the amount you started with?

reflectionPrompts.question: Where do you see people adding things together in real life around your home?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Explain orally that adding more items makes a collection grow larger.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about putting groceries away, adding scoops of cereal to a bowl, or setting forks on the dinner table.

documentationPrompt.instruction: Take a photo of your combined basket filled with treasures alongside your paper drawing of the math story.
documentationPrompt.suggestedCaption: We added [number] [item name] and [number] [item name] into our treasure basket to make [total] treasures in all!

extensions.title: Mystery Addition Guess
extensions.description: Place 4 items in the basket under a tea towel. Have your helper slip 2 more under the towel without showing you the inside. Count by tapping on your fingers to predict the total before lifting the towel to check!

extensions.title: Different Ways to Make 6
extensions.description: Gather 6 identical items. Try finding all the different ways to split them across your two plates (e.g., 5 and 1, 4 and 2, 3 and 3) before pouring them together.

safetyNotes: Adult helper recommended to guide object handling and supervise small counting pieces.
Ensure all selected household items are too large to present a choking hazard for young children.
Clear floor space to prevent slipping or tripping on stray toys or blocks.

problems.question: How many apples are two apples and three more apples?
problems.rationale: When you start with 2 apples and count 3 more, you count forward: 3, 4, 5. Putting a group of 2 and a group of 3 together makes 5 apples in all.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage learners to use their fingers or real counters to act out combining a group of 2 and a group of 3.
successCriteria: Combine two small groups of objects to find the total sum within 5.
Apply counting on or all-together strategies to solve basic addition situations.
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: What does the plus sign tell us to do?
problems.rationale: The plus sign (+) tells us to add or put groups together to find how many there are in all. In the math sentence 2 + 1 = 3, we join two objects and one more object to make three. Taking away is subtraction, which uses a minus sign instead.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce the physical motion of pushing two groups of counters together when introducing the plus symbol so learners connect the sign to joining sets.
successCriteria: Identify the plus sign (+) as the symbol for joining or putting groups together.
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.statement: When you put 2 toys and 1 toy together, you get a smaller number of toys.
problems.rationale: When you put toys together, addition makes the total amount get bigger, not smaller. If you start with 2 toys and add 1 more toy, you end up with 3 toys in total, which is more than 2.
problems.teachingNote: Kindergarteners sometimes confuse addition with subtraction or think that combining objects might make the group smaller. Use physical counters or toys to show that putting groups together always grows the total amount.
successCriteria: Understand that addition results in a larger total amount
Recognize the effect of combining two groups of objects
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: Adding more blocks makes the number get _____.
problems.rationale: When you add more blocks to a group, you have more than before. Putting things together makes the total amount grow bigger.
problems.teachingNote: Have students stack physical counters or blocks to watch the tower grow taller, reinforcing that addition means getting more.
successCriteria: Identify that adding items makes a quantity bigger
Understand that addition combines groups into a larger total
